newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BARCELONA'S STOICHKOV TAKES SWIPE AT REAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA'S STOICHKOV TAKES SWIPE AT REAL.

text.p: With just one game gone in the Spanish season, Barcelona's prodigal son Hristo Stoichkov is already in aggressive mood on and off the field.

After scoring twice in Barcelona's 4-2 win at Oviedo last week -- perfect preparation for this weekend's first home game with neighbours Espanyol -- the fiery Bulgarian striker took an early swipe at old rivals Real Madrid.
"Real won't win anything this year," he confidently predicted.

Ironically, Stoichkov, just back at Barcelona after a frustrating season in Italy with Parma, may yet be dropped for the Catalan derby at Nou Camp because of the return from international duty of influential Brazilian midfielder Giovanni.
Real, anxious to prove Stoichkov wrong after their scrappy 1-1 draw at Deportivo Coruna, entertain newly-promoted Hercules.
The 1995 champions will be boosted by the reappearance of ex-Ajax midfielder Clarence Seedorf, and are likely to use former German international goalkeeper Bodo Illgner, recently signed from Cologne.
The pressure on Illgner will be intense after Real fans at a training session pointedly applauded goals scored against him.
With the German between the posts, Spanish international reserve keeper Santiago Canizares will again be relegated to the bench while veteran Paco Buyo will watch the game from the stands.
A slip-up against Hercules -- a team with only one twentieth of Real's budget -- could turn fans, unhappy about the signing of Illgner, against coach Fabio Capello.
Champions Atletico Madrid will meet a familiar face when they travel to Compostela, the new home of Bulgarian forward Lyuboslav Penev.

Penev's replacement at Atletico, Argentine international striker Juan Eduardo Esnaider seems to be finding his form after moving across Madrid from Real, and will start the match despite picking up a heavy knock in a practice game on Wednesday.
Not so lucky was Atletico's Spanish international Jose Luis Caminero, who has a groin strain, while fellow midfielder Juan Vizcaino is doubtful after pulling up in training.
Despite the injuries Atletico start the game as clear favourites against a side who crashed 6-0 at Tenerife in their opening game after spending much of last year in second place.

Valencia, hoping to put defeat at Santander behind them in the home game against Real Sociedad, hope to see striker Romario on target -- the newly-signed Brazilian is three goals short of the 500 mark in his career.

A full house is expected at Sevilla for the home debut of Argentine defender Matias Almeyda against Zaragoza, while foreigners will dominate the Galician derby between Deportivo Coruna and Celta Vigo, with just one player from the province likely to make the starting line-ups.
Deportivo coach John Toshack will hope to ease the pressure after a week in which the league began an inquiry into insulting remarks he allegedly made after the game against Real Madrid.
